newsitem.title: INDIA: India April-June crude output rises to 8.40 mln T.
newsitem.headline: India April-June crude output rises to 8.40 mln T.

text.p: India's crude oil output during April-June 1997 rose to 8.40 million tonnes from 8.17 million tonnes in the same period in 1996, a Petroleum Ministry document obtained by Reuters on Thursday said.
The country produced 2.72 million tonnes of crude in June against the target of 2.73 million and compared with 2.62 million in June 1996.
Output in May 1997 was 2.87 million tonnes, slightly higher than the 2.81 million achieved in April, the document said.
State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp produced 7.20 million tonnes of crude between April and June 1997 and Oil India Ltd produced 0.75 million tonnes in the same period, the document said.
The private and joint venture firms contributed 0.45 million tonnes, the document said.

ONGC's output from oilfields in western Gujarat state dipped to 1.46 million tonnes against a target of 1.65 million on account of low reservoir potential in Gandhar and Ankaleshwar oilfields and poor crude offtake from Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Cambay projects.
Output from onshore blocks in northeastern state of Assam fell to 0.51 million tonnes against the targetted 0.61 million due to frequent power shutdowns, the document added.
The decline was compensated by higher output from ONGC's oilfields in Tamil Nadu and offshore blocks in Bombay High.
